title: Test score cutoff and college enrollment

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD).  

Why:  Admission policy gives automatic college entry to students whose standardized test score is at/above the cutoff = 0.5. Treatment status (treated = 1) jumps discontinuously at that score while everything else is assumed to change smoothly.  

Key assumptions  
1. Continuity: Potential outcomes (college–enrollment propensity) evolve smoothly in the running variable around the cutoff so any jump in y at 0.5 is attributable to treatment.  
2. No precise manipulation: Students cannot perfectly sort around 0.5; the density of running_var is continuous at the cutoff (testable with McCrary/rddensity).  
3. Stable unit treatment value (SUTVA) and no other policies kinked at the same score.  

Given these, the local average treatment effect at the cutoff identifies the causal impact of automatic admission on enrollment.



## 2. R Code
```r
############################################################
# Sharp RDD: automatic college admission & enrollment
# File: experiments/exp_b/data/s26_data.csv
############################################################

# 0) Packages ------------------------------------------------
needed <- c("readr", "rdrobust", "rddensity", "ggplot2")
sapply(needed, function(p) if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly=TRUE)) install.packages(p))
library(readr); library(rdrobust); library(rddensity); library(ggplot2)

# 1) Load data ----------------------------------------------
df <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s26_data.csv",
               show_col_types = FALSE)

# 2) Basic plot (optional visual check) ---------------------
ggplot(df, aes(x = running_var, y = y)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, colour = "red") +
  stat_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, colour = "blue") +
  labs(title = "College enrollment vs. test score",
       x = "Standardized test score (running variable)",
       y = "Enrollment proxy (y)")

# 3) Main RDD estimate: rdrobust with data–driven bandwidth --
cutoff <- 0.5
rd_main <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff,
                    p = 1, kernel = "triangular")  # local linear

cat("=== Main RDD result (local linear, optimal bw) ===\n")
print(summary(rd_main)$coef)

# Extract point estimate (τ̂) and 95% CI
tau_hat  <- rd_main$coef[1,1]
se_hat   <- rd_main$coef[1,2]
ci_low   <- tau_hat - 1.96*se_hat
ci_high  <- tau_hat + 1.96*se_hat
cat(sprintf("\nLATE at cutoff: %.4f  (95%% CI: [%.4f , %.4f])\n",
            tau_hat, ci_low, ci_high))

# 4) Robustness checks --------------------------------------

## 4.1 McCrary density test (manipulation)
dens <- rddensity(df$running_var, c = cutoff)
cat("\n=== McCrary density test ===\n")
print(summary(dens))

## 4.2 Alternative (narrower) bandwidth 0.20
rd_narrow <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff,
                      p = 1, h = 0.20, kernel = "triangular")
cat("\n=== RDD with bandwidth h = 0.20 ===\n")
print(summary(rd_narrow)$coef[1,])

## 4.3 Higher–order polynomial (quadratic) with optimal bw
rd_quad <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff,
                    p = 2, kernel = "triangular")
cat("\n=== RDD with quadratic control (p = 2) ===\n")
print(summary(rd_quad)$coef[1,])

# 5) Output tidy numeric table ------------------------------
results <- data.frame(
  Specification = c("Main_optimal_bw", "Bandwidth_0.20", "Quadratic"),
  Estimate      = c(rd_main$coef[1,1],
                    rd_narrow$coef[1,1],
                    rd_quad$coef[1,1]),
  Std_Error     = c(rd_main$coef[1,2],
                    rd_narrow$coef[1,2],
                    rd_quad$coef[1,2])
)
cat("\n=== Summary table ===\n")
print(results, row.names = FALSE)
```

The script  
• imports the data,  
• visualises the discontinuity,  
• obtains the local linear RDD estimate with `rdrobust`,  
• reports the treatment effect and confidence interval,  
• performs a McCrary density test,  
• re-estimates with a tighter bandwidth and with a quadratic polynomial, and  
• prints a compact results table.



## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Positive. Automatic admission should raise the likelihood of actually enrolling.  

Magnitude: Around +0.18 – +0.25 (18–25 percentage-point increase).  
Rationale: Crossing the threshold converts uncertain applicants → guaranteed acceptance, which is a large incentive but not all treated students will take it (some may attend different institutions or choose not to enroll). Therefore we expect a sizeable yet far-from-unity jump in enrollment at the cutoff.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Sharp RDD — test score cutoff; continuity of running variable required; McCrary density test
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Scoring above cutoff significantly increases college enrollment
